CA.quote: On January 1, 2023, the contractor license bond, bond of qualifying individual, and disciplinary bond, increased to $25,000 as a result of Senate Bill 607.
CA.note: Required to issue, reactivate or renew an active license. A separate $25,000 bond of qualifying individual can apply to an RME or RMO, and an LLC also needs a $100,000 worker bond.

WA.quote: a Washington Continuous Contractor Surety Bond in the amount of $30,000 for general contractors and $15,000 for specialty contractors
WA.note: Raised on July 1, 2024 (from $12,000 and $6,000). Contractors with unpaid final judgments post more under WAC 296-200A-030.

OR.note: Amounts since January 1, 2024. A contractor with both residential and commercial endorsements posts two bonds.

NV.quote: the bond can vary in amount from $1,000 to $500,000 based on the type of license, monetary limit, past, present or future financial responsibility, experience, and character of the applicant
NV.note: The Board sets the amount when it approves the license, from the monetary limit and the applicant's finances. Residential contractors taking deposits above the AB 39 threshold also post a $100,000 consumer protection bond.

AZ.quote: Residential Specialty Contractors | Less than $375,000 | $4,250; $375,000 or more | $7,500
AZ.note: Set by license type and estimated annual volume. Residential contractors also pay into the Recovery Fund or post a second $200,000 bond.

FL.statute: Fla. Stat. ch. 489; Fla. Admin. Code r. 61G4-15
FL.quote: Bonds must be in the amount of $100,000.
FL.note: No general contractor license bond statewide. A $100,000 bond applies to a Financially Responsible Officer, and a bond is one way to meet the financial test when the credit score is under 660. Cities and counties may require local bonds.
